security_audit.summary: Most static code-execution alerts were markdown code fence false positives, not Ruby backtick execution. Confirmed issues remain around cluster-changing setup commands, direct remote manifest application, and a Flux install command that pipes network content to sudo bash. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Remote install script with root privileges
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-sudo Flux install command with a pinned package, checksum verification, or manual review step.
Pin exact ArgoCD release URLs and tell users to inspect manifests before applying them to a cluster.

remediation.issue: Production auto-sync with prune in examples
remediation.suggestion: Change production examples to manual sync or approval-gated sync. Reserve automated prune and selfHeal for lower environments.

remediation.issue: Repository token shown as a command argument
remediation.suggestion: Use credential prompts, environment-specific secret stores, or documented secure token handling instead of command-line password arguments.

content.value_statement: Kubernetes delivery becomes hard to audit when cluster state drifts from Git. This skill guides ArgoCD and Flux workflows for declarative, reconciled deployments.
actual_capabilities: Explains OpenGitOps principles for Kubernetes delivery.
Shows ArgoCD application structure and app-of-apps patterns.
Outlines Flux bootstrap, GitRepository, and Kustomization resources.
Documents sync policies, retries, health checks, and sync windows.
Covers canary, blue-green, external secrets, and sealed secrets patterns.
Provides troubleshooting commands for ArgoCD sync and drift issues.
limitations: Requires existing Kubernetes cluster access and repository permissions.
Does not replace production change approval or release governance.
Examples use placeholder organizations, repositories, and domains.
Installation commands should be reviewed before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a GitOps layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a GitOps repository layout for a Kubernetes team with staging and production environments. Include folders, ownership boundaries, and release flow.

prompt_templates.title: Create ArgoCD applications
prompt_templates.prompt: Design ArgoCD Application resources for three services in one cluster. Include project boundaries, sync policy choices, and rollback notes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Flux and ArgoCD
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Flux and ArgoCD for a regulated Kubernetes platform. Focus on reconciliation, secrets, approvals, observability, and team workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design multi-cluster delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-cluster GitOps workflow with progressive delivery, production approval gates, external secrets, and drift monitoring.

output_examples.input: Plan GitOps for staging and production clusters.
output_examples.output: A repository layout with environment folders, ownership notes, promotion flow, sync policy choices, and rollback checks.

output_examples.input: Review an ArgoCD production sync policy.
output_examples.output: A risk review that highlights auto-sync, prune behavior, approval gates, rollback readiness, and monitoring requirements.

output_examples.input: Choose between ArgoCD and Flux for a platform team.
output_examples.output: A comparison covering bootstrap style, reconciliation model, operational controls, secret management, and team adoption impact.

best_practices: Use manual approvals or sync windows for production changes.
Keep secrets out of Git by using sealed or external secret managers.
Pin installation sources and inspect manifests before applying them.
anti_patterns: Do not enable production auto-sync with prune before approval controls exist.
Do not paste access tokens into shared commands or documentation.
Do not apply remote manifests without reviewing the source and version.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy applications by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for ArgoCD and Flux workflows.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers ArgoCD, Flux, Kubernetes manifests, sync policies, and secret management patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with production approvals?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes approval gates, sync windows, and safer production sync choices.

faq.question: Does it include secret management guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses External Secrets Operator and Sealed Secrets patterns.

faq.question: Are the repository URLs ready to use?
faq.answer: No. The examples use placeholder organizations and repositories that users must replace.

faq.question: Should installation commands be run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review commands, versions, and permissions before running them against a cluster.
